x: Uncle Secretary offers congratulations to Knifton on his walking in the Club Open Walk and if he will look in the Laundry cart he might find another 30 Secs, to George Pepper, if he looks behind the Gas Meter he might win a Veterans 220yds, to Bob, if he looks behind the flushing cistern he might fi…
Probably the 4 hours train journey upset the form of some, especially Knifton who had the disturbing experience of travelling by the wrong train.

A Martin was first off and was never headed, while Knifton who returned fastest time could get no nearer than fourth. In our own "Open," we expect the support of all our active walkers, and hope to be well supported as usual by other clubs, on November 26th.
Knifton has been forced to resign the positions of Hon.
For a moment all seemed lost, but Rathbone and Knifton, we knew, were walking well and might be expected to make up some arrears. At this point they were 36th and 49th respectively.

…nd, as for processions, have you tried to picture the finish of the Club 20 mile championship as a handicap with Field, Knifton and Saunders leading, and Green and Cooper at scratch vainly trying to catch them?…
Joe Flower, our mile champion, had to run a hundred yards in this event. In the Walk, we were represented by Knifton, Dodkin and L.
In the Walk, in which Len Fletcher suffered disqualification, Scamell gained a A.A.A. standard medal and Knifton a Southern standard. Others to gain Southern standard medals were G.
King, Knifton, and Rathbone. Green has a good chance for individual, as well as Team honours, and I hope Knifton will soon settle down to serious training.

Saunders and Knifton both started very steadily. At 5 miles the order was almost the same, Bidgood alone having fallen back through too fast a start, but the gap set up by the three leaders was larger.
Meanwhile Jack Field had been having a rough time, and Knifton and Rathbone appeared to be too far behind to have a chance of scoring for the team, as they did last year.
King managed to keep another Ashcombe representative out of second place, but as Knifton's interest in the race had been curtailed, team honours went deservedly to Ashcombe A.C.
Hillier, who was walking with Knifton in 7th position, appeared to be walking very strongly at this point and seemed certain to win the handicap if he could last.
Two miles walk.—1, Knifton (660); 2, James (260); 3, Coton (560).
Goswell at the bottom of Copse Hill and Mr. and Mrs. Knifton, Marlene and Celia around the course.
